# Decisions: stale-session-signals

- 2026-08-13T15:02:20.308Z — rule: **No signal may be the only way a session can learn something — anything a hook line reports must stay derivable by a session that simply runs `sofar status` or `sofar review`.** — chose **Three host tiers, stated in SPEC §Host tiers and binding on every future surface. Tier 1 (hooks + a live-session registry — Claude Code) gets everything including the lines whose content is an ADDRESS. Tier 2 (hooks, no registry) gets every signal except those, rendering silence rather than a name-less variant. Tier 3 (no hooks — Codex, Grok, OpenCode, the AGENTS.md dialect) gets nothing automatically, and reaches the same facts by asking: `sofar status` and `sofar review`. The invariant: no signal may be the ONLY way to learn something.** over Rendering a degraded address-less line on hosts with no registry ("another record's work landed" with nobody named), and the opposite error of treating the ping as the mechanism and leaving non-Claude hosts with no shipping signal at all — which is what D13 was written to prevent by sequencing the ping after the ref-gated read. because The address IS the actionable content of those lines; without it the reader is told something they can do nothing about, and a line that cannot be acted on teaches them to skim the ones that can. Silence is honest there. Stating the tiers explicitly is what stops the next surface being designed for Claude Code by accident — D12 already had to correct exactly that once, when the review packet named a slash command as the instruction. And the invariant keeps the asymmetry from becoming a truth gap: Tier 3 is slower and must ask, but nothing is unreachable there.
